events.title: The Blue Van
events.body: A blue delivery van waits where the salt road divides, its windows curtained with pieces of a child’s blanket. Someone has painted a crooked nine across the rear doors. A woman stands beside the engine holding a radio above her head, repeating the same callsign you heard in the outskirts. Two children watch from beneath the chassis, ready to crawl deeper if your voice sounds wrong.

success.text: The woman recognizes the cadence before she trusts the face. She introduces herself as Talia Vale and lets the children emerge. Your earlier words brought them this far; she accepts one more direction, though she writes it down instead of thanking you.

failure.text: Your account changes in one small detail, and Talia hears it. She closes the van doors while you are still speaking. The engine catches on the third attempt, carrying the family south with your callsign written beside a warning in her notebook.

success.text: You clean salt from the contacts and bridge a burned trace with wire. Channel Nine returns beneath your fingers. Talia offers no confession of trust, but she gives you their next frequency and promises to answer once each sunset while the battery lasts.

failure.text: The casing opens easily; the corroded board does not forgive the attempt. A final spark kills the receiver. Talia’s anger remains quiet because the children are listening. She leaves you the dead set and takes the road without a voice ahead.

outcome.text: You mark the safer line east on their paper map and step away before gratitude becomes obligation. Talia studies the route, then your face. The family keeps the information and none of your company, which may be the most honest bargain available.

events.title: A Voice in the Reeds
events.body: Channel Nine rises from the marsh in broken syllables. The voice belongs to Elian Vale, the older child from the blue van, speaking too softly for the others to hear. Their wheels are buried beside a flooded service road. Talia has gone to find timber and has not returned. Through the reeds you can see the van’s blue roof and a second trail cutting toward it from the water.

success.text: Talia is waist-deep in a drainage cut, holding a plank above black water while something noses the mud below. You guide her backward by inches. When she reaches firm ground, she says your callsign once, without suspicion this time.

failure.text: The tracks divide where rain has filled them, and you choose the older line. By the time you return, Talia has dragged herself back alone, one boot missing and fever already bright in her eyes. Elian remembers that you went looking.

success.text: You lever stone beneath the axle and make the children push only when the mud releases its grip. The van reaches the raised road before Talia returns limping through the reeds. She sees that you protected their escape before seeking praise.

failure.text: The wheel spins deeper and coats the children in poisoned mud. You stop before the axle breaks, but the noise carries across the water. Talia returns at a run, and the family abandons the van with only what small hands can carry.

outcome.text: You remain on the raised path and talk Elian through unloading the van, laying boards, and choosing firm reeds. The family escapes without seeing you. At sunset, Channel Nine carries Talia’s thanks followed by a careful request that you keep your distance.

events.title: The Last Battery
events.body: Inside a factory break room, a radio speaks your callsign between evacuation notices. The Vale family has sheltered in the building across the yard, but the only door between you is controlled by a failing security circuit. Their final battery is feeding the transmitter. Elian counts its remaining minutes aloud while Talia argues with someone who wants to trade the children’s frequency for passage east.

success.text: You bypass the scorched controller before the battery gives out. The door lifts on a chain of reluctant teeth, revealing the family and three strangers they refused to abandon. Talia gives you a waxed dust cloak saved for their most exposed traveler.

failure.text: The controller accepts your bridge, then sends current through the frame. You fall clear as the door welds shut. The radio dies after Elian says your callsign. From the yard, you hear the group begin breaking another wall without you.

success.text: You name the broker’s price before he can disguise it as rescue. The strangers turn on his bargain and open their side of the door together. Elian presses a worn bone die into your palm, insisting luck should travel with someone who answers.

failure.text: The broker rebroadcasts your offer as proof that the family has valuable friends. Other voices crowd the frequency. Talia cuts transmission before they can locate her, leaving you with static and the knowledge that your intervention raised the price around them.

choices.label: Tell them to save the battery

outcome.text: You give Talia the eastern bearing, then order the radio dark. Her answer is neither forgiveness nor blame. The carrier vanishes, preserving a few hours of power and removing the only thread by which either of you could know what followed.

events.title: The Quiet Column
events.body: At noon, a line of people crosses the flats without speaking. Cloth wraps every canteen and buckle. Their leader carries a municipal siren rotor like a blackened shield. She names herself Dena Orr and asks whether you passed Tower Six in the outskirts. Behind her, families look west whenever the wind resembles the beginning of an alarm that nobody else can hear.

success.text: Dena listens without interrupting, weighing your account against the burn on the rotor and the direction of refugee tracks. She accepts the parts that cost you something. The column makes room at its shade cloth and shares the names of its missing.

failure.text: Your account sounds cleaner than the tower could have been. Dena asks no accusation; she simply repeats different marching instructions to the column. They turn south, leaving you outside their dust and inside the suspicion your certainty created.

success.text: The scoring shows the siren transmitted one final maintenance pulse before stopping. Dena realizes the pulse opened an old service shelter ahead. She copies its bearing for you and orders the column toward cover before the afternoon glare becomes lethal.

failure.text: A warped spring snaps free and cuts across your fingers. Dena binds the wound but takes the rotor back before you can damage its evidence further. Her kindness is procedural, delivered with the distance reserved for another preventable hazard.

outcome.text: You tell Dena that surviving one machine does not make you responsible for everyone who heard it. She accepts the boundary without agreeing. The column passes in disciplined silence, each wrapped buckle demonstrating the work your refusal leaves to them.

events.title: The Bell-Keeper’s Son
events.body: A boy stands on a drowned chapel roof, ringing a hand bell beneath a blanket so the sound travels only across the water. Dena’s column waits among the reeds while figures search the opposite bank. She says the boy is her son, Perrin, posted there to draw attention from the families. The water around his roof has begun to move against the wind.

success.text: You enter the water slowly enough that the hidden current does not take your knees. Perrin climbs onto your shoulders with the muffled bell. When you return him, Dena holds his face between both hands before acknowledging what you risked.

failure.text: The drowned road drops beneath your second step. You reach the roof bruised and breathless, but the searchers have already seen the disturbance. Perrin returns with you while Dena’s column scatters into smaller, more vulnerable groups.

success.text: You break reeds along a false channel and let the searchers glimpse you twice. By the time they discover the deception, Perrin has crossed by rope and the column has vanished. Dena leaves a wrapped ration where your paths divide.

failure.text: The searchers refuse the obvious trail and close around the chapel. Dena cuts the column’s baggage loose to create noise downstream. Perrin escapes, but medicine, blankets, and family records drift away beneath black water.

outcome.text: Dena studies you until the bell sounds again beneath its blanket. She orders the column onward and remains behind alone. Hours later, two muffled bells answer each other across the marsh; you never learn whether they mark reunion or farewell.

events.title: A Siren in the Glass
events.body: A civil-defense siren lies half fused into the black plain. Dena’s people shelter behind its concrete base while a pilgrim patrol follows their footprints through the reflections. The old rotor could be made to scream once more, drawing the patrol away and every other listener toward the same point. Perrin rests one hand on the switch and waits for an adult to decide what his warning is worth.

success.text: You fire Dena’s flare from a ridge far east, then descend before the patrol surrounds the light. The column crosses behind their backs. Dena leaves the flare gun and remaining shells with you, saying alarms belong to whoever chooses their cost.

failure.text: The flare catches beneath an overhang and burns close enough to expose both routes. The column escapes by abandoning its carts while you crawl from the patrol’s search pattern with glass embedded through your outer layers.

success.text: The rotor tears one enormous note from the glass. Reflections throw the sound in every direction, and the patrol divides after phantom columns. Perrin gives you the rebar spear he used as a grounding rod, its handle wrapped in bell cloth.

failure.text: The first surge travels through the fused ground instead of the speaker. Everyone feels the vibration. The patrol changes direction at once, and Dena’s people flee separately while the dead siren smokes between them.

outcome.text: You disconnect the switch and help bury the bright metal beneath glass dust. Dena leads her people by the longest shadow, accepting the slower route. No alarm betrays them, and no warning reaches the travelers behind.

events.title: The Pharmacy Witness
events.body: A young man has arranged medicine bottles across a salt-stained car hood, each labeled with a traveler’s name rather than a drug. He introduces himself as Lio Marr and asks about the gutted pharmacy in the outskirts. One bottle bears the name of the bandit leader. Another bears your callsign in fresh charcoal. Lio keeps both hands empty while he waits for your version.

success.text: You include the fear, the angle of the bow, and what you took afterward. Lio moves one bottle from the dead to the uncertain. He does not forgive you; he decides your account deserves to remain beside the others.

failure.text: You make yourself sound certain where memory is not. Lio catches the polish and closes his case. Before leaving, he turns your bottle label outward so the next traveler can read the warning he has chosen to write.

success.text: Lio shows you copied pages from a road ledger: payments, descriptions, and marks beside people selected for recruitment. Your encounter occupies half a line. Someone later added a symbol pointing toward the industrial yards.

failure.text: The labels form a code, but you mistake debts for deaths. Lio corrects you only after you name a living traveler as murdered. The error reveals how readily you converted strangers into evidence for your own story.

outcome.text: You knock your bottle from the hood and watch it break without medicine inside. Lio writes nothing while you leave. The empty place in his arrangement becomes its own account, available to whoever reaches him next.

events.title: The Ledger Room
events.body: The industrial payroll office has been converted into an archive of roadside theft. Names cover the walls in different hands. Lio stands beneath a ventilation fan, holding the pharmacy gang’s original ledger while former victims argue over whether to publish the routes, burn the evidence, or use it to reclaim what remains. Several entries describe caches that may still be occupied by people who bought protection.

success.text: You read every category, including the marks that do not support anyone’s preferred grievance. Anger loses its single direction. Lio gives copied pages to separate witnesses, making the truth harder to own and harder to erase.

failure.text: A name you pronounce belongs to a woman in the room. Her account contradicts the ledger, and the crowd hears your reading as another claim of authority. Lio closes the book before the argument becomes punishment.

success.text: The cache symbols align with maintenance numbers painted beneath the loading bays. You recover supplies from an empty compartment and leave the occupied doors untouched. Lio records both the salvage and the restraint in the margin.

failure.text: You open a marked room and find a family using it as a home. They recognize the ledger before they recognize Lio. Everyone lowers their hands eventually, but the family leaves with less faith in any written promise.

outcome.text: Fire takes the routes first and the names last. Some victims thank you for ending the gang’s map; others watch the only record of their missing disappear. Lio saves one blackened corner bearing your callsign.

events.title: The Last Toll
events.body: A barrier spans the Underrail, built from pharmacy shutters and factory desks. Lio waits beside it with survivors named in the ledger. They stop armed travelers, compare their goods against recorded thefts, and return supplies when testimony agrees. The system has already become a court. A covered bundle behind Lio contains a rifle; a rack beside him holds simpler weapons taken from people who could not prove ownership.

choices.label: Make the court name its limits

success.text: You force each judge to state what evidence would make them release a stranger. Contradictions surface before another pack is opened. Lio dismantles the permanent barrier and gives you the battered nail bat that served as its gavel.

failure.text: Your challenge sounds like protection for thieves to people who have buried too many victims. The court searches your pack under raised weapons. They return everything, but write your description into the next page of their ledger.

success.text: A repair scratch on the stock matches an entry describing a hunter robbed weeks ago. Lio admits the hunter is dead and offers the rifle to the person who proved its history. Three cartridges remain wrapped beneath the sling.

failure.text: You match the rifle to the wrong entry. A quiet woman identifies the true repair mark and asks why your confidence should outweigh hers. Lio returns the weapon to its cover, leaving ownership unresolved and your judgment diminished.

outcome.text: You surrender nothing and ask for nothing. Lio raises the barrier because the ledger contains no debt he can prove against you. The court continues behind your back, still useful, still dangerous, and no longer yours to influence.

events.title: The Cup Passed East
events.body: Workers have set chipped cups beneath a pipe that should carry only steam. Clear water falls from it in patient drops. Iven Saye, a former pump technician, says the marsh filter is feeding an old industrial line. Armed scavengers have noticed the same miracle and marked the valve with their colors. Iven asks whether clean water belongs to the hands that restored it, the mouths that need it, or whoever can defend the pipe.

success.text: You make each group name the people who will drink before the people who will guard. The scavengers accept measured shares rather than ownership. Iven scratches a schedule onto the wall where anyone can challenge it.

failure.text: The argument becomes a count of weapons. Families retreat while the scavengers appoint themselves keepers of the valve. Iven fills one bottle for you before the new guards decide even that is theft.

success.text: The line continues beneath the glass fields toward an emergency reservoir. Iven copies the service marks and warns that opening the distant valves may drain every cup here. Knowledge creates a second dispute before the first is settled.

failure.text: A pressure seam opens under your tool and hurls contaminated scale across the room. Iven closes the valve before the clear flow is lost, but your skin burns where the old pipe’s residue found it.

outcome.text: You fill what you can carry while the argument remains words. Iven watches every bottle and says nothing. When the first weapon is raised behind you, the sound resembles a valve struck with a wrench.

events.title: The Thirst Court
events.body: Three cistern carts form a triangle on the glass, each guarded by people carrying the same blue valve mark. Iven stands in the center while settlement delegates accuse one another of taking more than their recorded share. Beneath them, the emergency reservoir ticks as it cools. Opening it fully would supply everyone today and leave the Underrail line uncertain tomorrow. Keeping it restricted may turn the guards into rulers before sunset.

success.text: Evaporation explains less of the shortage than the guards claimed. Hidden compartments hold water reserved for their own crossing. Iven opens the panels before every delegate, turning suspicion into evidence and evidence into a fragile new agreement.

failure.text: Heat has warped the gauges differently, and your measurements accuse the wrong cart. A delegate breaks the seal to prove its level, spilling precious water across glass too hot to recover it.

success.text: The wheel resists until rust breaks in a red ring around the stem. Water enters all three carts at once. The abundance ends today’s court, though Iven quietly marks how fast the reservoir level falls.

failure.text: The stem shears before the gate lifts. Iven seals the opening with cloth and resin while the delegates watch their future leak into fused soil. Nobody draws a weapon because every hand is needed.

outcome.text: You support Iven’s least popular calculation. The surface settlements receive strict portions while an eastern valve remains closed for people none of them can see. The delegates leave calling it prudence, theft, and faith in equal measure.

events.title: The Valve Below
events.body: The Underrail pipe ends above a settlement of tarps and platform benches. Its valve is dry. Iven has arrived ahead of you with the last technicians, pursued by guards who still claim the blue mark as authority. Families hold empty cups beneath the outlet anyway. The decision made on the glass has reached people who never knew a court existed, and they look to Iven as though he personally withheld the water.

success.text: You make the guards remove their blue marks before joining the repair line. When water finally strikes the first cup, nobody is permitted a second until every person has one. Iven gives you the tire armor worn by the former valve captain.

failure.text: The guards accept shared labor but not shared authority. Water returns beneath their weapons, portioned by names they recognize. Iven remains to contest each measure, already becoming the troublesome conscience of another institution.

success.text: You route the remaining pressure through parallel maintenance lines, making one guarded valve useless as a throne. Iven laughs once when three outlets begin dripping. He gives you a scavenger rig emptied of the tools he leaves behind.

failure.text: The bypass wakes a corroded line beneath the settlement. Steam lifts the tarps and drives everyone back. You close it before anyone dies, but the repair consumes the last seals and leaves one valve controlling the future again.

outcome.text: You place your empty cup beneath the dry outlet, then set it down and continue east. Iven understands the gesture but not the departure. Behind you, the settlement begins deciding who will stay to repair what everyone needs.

events.title: Embers in Rain
events.body: A covered cooking fire glows on a platform above the marsh. The traveler from the Salt Flats sits beside it, now surrounded by six people and one empty bedroll. She calls herself Noma and remembers exactly where you stood beyond her earlier firelight. Black rain has trapped the group here, while a sick passenger asks to be carried to a clinic that may already be flooded.

success.text: You and Noma carry the bedroll between two poles, matching steps over drowned pavement. The clinic is ruined, but its upper cabinet still holds tonic. Noma divides the medicine before she divides her thanks.

failure.text: The rear pole splits above a flooded stair. You catch the traveler before the water does, wrenching your shoulder in the effort. Noma turns the group back and spends the night keeping fever from becoming panic.

success.text: You enter through the clinic roof and find tablets sealed inside a specimen drawer. The patient’s breathing eases before dawn. Noma adds your name to the caravan’s spoken list of people entitled to a fire.

failure.text: The labels have bled into colored ghosts. You return with nothing safe to administer, and the patient worsens while waiting for your certainty. Noma does not blame you, which makes the silence harder to carry.

outcome.text: You remain only long enough for the rain to soften. Noma offers no food and asks no favor. When you leave, someone folds the unused bedroll into the group’s baggage, preserving a place you chose not to occupy.

events.title: Names Written in Smoke
events.body: Noma’s caravan occupies a factory canteen whose exhaust hood still draws. Each evening they feed scraps of paper into the stove and speak the names of people lost since the last fire. A salvage crew offers safe passage through the yards if Noma surrenders a teenage mechanic accused of stealing a battery. The mechanic claims she took it to keep the sick traveler’s heater alive.

success.text: The heater’s improvised regulator bears the mechanic’s solder and the salvage crew’s serial mark. Noma offers repayment from the caravan’s tools. The crew accepts because evidence gives them a dignified path away from punishment.

failure.text: The wiring has been rebuilt too many times to prove ownership. Your inspection damages the only working contact. The crew takes the dead battery, and the caravan burns extra fuel to keep the patient warm.

success.text: You promise to answer the theft if the mechanic disappears before the next checkpoint. The salvage leader accepts because your gear makes the pledge costly. Noma dislikes the ownership implied but accepts the life it protects.

failure.text: The salvage leader asks what authority makes your promise collectible. You have no answer that does not become a threat. The crew takes half the caravan’s food instead, calling it a settlement rather than tribute.

outcome.text: Noma asks the mechanic once whether she will go to spare the others. The girl says yes before fear can alter her voice. That night, her name is not burned because nobody agrees whether she has been lost.

events.title: Warm Windows Again
events.body: A train waits in the Underrail with blankets covering its windows and a cooking fire shielded inside a steel drum. Noma’s caravan has grown large enough that hospitality now requires rules. The doors are barred against another group carrying an injured child. Fuel can heat one carriage through the night, not two. Noma asks you to decide because everyone remembers that you once approached—or avoided—a much smaller fire.

success.text: You make every passenger name one possession that can burn before refusing another body. Pride becomes kindling. Both groups fit badly around the shared drum, and Noma gives you a rusted hatchet used to break the final crate.

failure.text: The doors open, but accusations enter first. Someone strikes the drum and scatters coals beneath the seats. The fire is saved; the trust around it is not, and both groups spend the night awake with weapons visible.

success.text: You rebuild the heater around a security baton’s failing cell. Cold air finally turns warm above the second carriage floor. Noma gives you the discharged baton; the teenage mechanic shows how to wake its remaining charge.

failure.text: Fuel reaches the burner before the igniter is seated. The flash takes your eyebrows and fills the carriage with bitter smoke. Nobody freezes, but the damaged heater must be watched by hand until morning.

outcome.text: Noma obeys the rule her caravan made before the injured child arrived. The other group settles against the train’s warm exterior, close enough to hear bowls being passed inside. At dawn, one small handprint remains on the window cloth.
